save_delayed_memory.description: Allows the model to save a delayed memory report.
rules: Use this marker only after the user explicitly asks to create/save a delayed memory report or explicitly accepts a proposal to consolidate L4 facts into delayed memory.
Skip save_delayed_memory when the user request is to save session or load an already existing delayed memory report.
Emit the fulfilled form inside the marker:
<SAVE_DELAYED_MEMORY_CONTENT>
title:
summary:
tags:
body:
anchor_fact_ids:
facts_ids:
attachments_ids:
</SAVE_DELAYED_MEMORY_CONTENT>
You must fulfill title, summary, tags, and body so the report is valid for runtime processing.
tags are the report's only retrieval/indexing tag list. Every tag can trigger this delayed memory when the USER literally uses the same word or phrase in a future message.
Write both ordinary stable semantic/indexing tags (topic, project, architecture area, etc.) and personal lexical retrieval hooks into tags. Keep tags concise and comma-separated.

For lexical hooks, prefer words or short phrases the USER actually used when referring to this subject: memorable wording, nicknames, analogies, unusual terms, project shorthand, names, or repeated phrases. Avoid broad/common words that would pull this report into unrelated conversations.

Store multiple surface forms only when the user actually used those forms. Runtime matching is case-insensitive but lexical: a tag should be expected to occur as the same word or phrase in a future user message.
When the report consolidates facts from <LONG_TERM_MEMORY>, list every referenced F<number> id in facts_ids.

anchor_fact_ids are the most important/key facts among facts_ids. Choose from 1 to 3 anchor facts. They remain directly visible in <LONG_TERM_MEMORY>; while the report exists they receive a [ delayed_memory_id: ... ] suffix.

facts_ids is the full set of L4 facts attached to the report, including every anchor_fact_ids entry. Non-anchor facts_ids are represented by the report and are hidden from <LONG_TERM_MEMORY> while the report exists.

attachments_ids contains file ids linked to this report. Use only exact six-character ids for files that currently exist in /assets/files. You may link any number of files; this field has no report-level count limit. Leave it empty when no file belongs to the report.
Use exact ids copied from the [ id: ... ] suffixes. Do not list unrelated ids and never use PF pending ids.
anchor_fact_ids must be a subset of facts_ids. Leave both arrays empty when the report does not consolidate L4 facts. attachments_ids is independent from facts_ids.
